correctness.rationale: For k<=n-1, simultaneous positive labels form a partial Latin square, and the negatives can be filled greedily without their forbidden symbols using at most k-1 previous-symbol exclusions plus one forbidden value. The published Smetaniuk completion theorem then realizes every Boolean trace. A full Latin row gives the sharp size-n obstruction. At n=3, each of 12 Latin square hypotheses contains four of the 27 possible entries; the Hamming-weight saturation argument forces every nonzero pattern once for shattered triples and yields precisely 216 Latin triangles. All 270 compatible pairs are shattered; there are 108 maximal pairs, no shattered fours. Two distinct constructions of the 12 squares and the edge-triangle incidence complex give rank(d2)=133 over F2, betti1=111, betti2=83. The Python checker further verifies all 25920 compatible triples at n=4. Original finite source paths were inspected and both programs executed. These computations have finite, explicit, reproducible domains and are not used as a proof of the infinite-n completion theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2016 Hatami-Qian paper treats exactly the same family of Latin squares as subsets of [n]^3, but its published VC statements are asymptotic bounds and its full inspected text does not state an exact n=3 shattering face complex or homology. The 2017 Luria-Simkin paper treats support thresholds for random Latin boxes, not trace shattering. Smetaniuk already proved the completion theorem used for low-size supports; this input is not attributed as new. Published mathematical records on the complex of all partial Latin squares and on finite-variable Latin-square incidence are not the Boolean shattering complex of all completed Latin squares; their currently accessible summaries show a different object and no implication of these exact Betti ranks. The new contribution is the combined exact n=3 geometric and homological boundary, with the sharp low-size Boolean trace formulation. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Unindexed finite Latin-square trace computations could already contain the order-three polynomial and binary Betti numbers.
The two closest published indexed geometric results were comparable by their summaries only, not full documents; their stated objects nevertheless differ.
The original 1981 proof of Smetaniuk theorem was not re-read, although its exact statement was verified in a later journal.

value.rationale: The exact low-order boundary is motivated by the same Latin-square learning class studied in a primary paper, and the sharp <=n-1 universal shattering guarantee resolves every labelled support in that range rather than a scalar extremum. At the smallest order where the guarantee does not settle triples, the precise geometric obstruction and nonpure maximal-face classification are given, with 111 mod-two one-cycles and 83 two-cycles. These are natural combinatorial invariants of the same hypothesis family and are not known-table recomputations in the literature checked; they support studying local completion obstructions and topology of learning traces. The result does not claim a new general completion theorem or universal higher-degree VC bound.
